AbstractText.Label: STUDY OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To determine if right-left pelvic pain orientation exists in all patients, and to estimate the frequency of pain referral patterns in the pelvis.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: Prospective, nonrandomized trial (Canadian Task Force classification II-1).

AbstractText.Label: PATIENTS
AbstractText.content: One hundred consecutive women with no pain undergoing tubal sterilization or investigation of infertility (group A) were compared with 225 women with chronic pelvic pain of greater than 6 months' duration (group B).

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTION
AbstractText.content: Patient-assisted laparoscopy with intravenous conscious sedation and pelvic pain mapping.

AbstractText.Label: MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Of women in group A, 69% had correct right-left orientation, 18% had pain perceived on the opposite side of the abdomen, and 31% had pain referred to another location in the abdomen. The results were similar in women in group B, 65% of whom had correct orientation, 15% had pain perceived on the opposite side of the abdomen, and 35% had pain referred to another location.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: This demonstrates the need to ask on which side a woman feels pain during physical examination. It is not correct to assume that an answer of "yes" means the same side of the pelvis that is being examined. Patient-assisted laparoscopy and pelvic pain mapping are excellent in correlating the symptom with the pathology.
